children.text: Filling out the DS-160 is one of the most important parts of the
US

visa process, since the DS-160 is the application that gathers information about the details of your trip and about yourself. It's based on your interview and your DS-160 that the consular officer makes their decision, which is why filling it out with precise accuracy is essential.
Small mistakes can significantly delay the processing of your visa application. To avoid such a situation, take a look at the 5 most common mistakes and how to avoid them.
1. Entering Personal Information Incorrectly

In the DS-160, you enter information such as your first name (in Latin script), last name (in Latin script), gender, passport number, nationality, and date of birth. When you receive the visa, this information is transferred to your passport, and incorrectly entered information can put your visa at risk or cause problems when crossing the border.
So make sure your personal data is transferred into the application exactly as it appears on your official documents, such as your passport.
2. Inaccurate Information

When filling out the visa application, it's important that all information be accurate, up to date, and complete. Any inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated information may raise doubts about your application and become a reason for visa refusal.

Make sure your employment history matches exactly the information you can confirm with official documents. In addition, list all your visits to other countries in detail, especially to the US, and don't forget to include information about your family members.
3. Uploading an Incorrect Photo
Following the standards for the visa photo is crucial. A photo with the wrong size, lighting, or quality can become a reason for your visa application to be refused.

It's essential that the photo for your visa application be recent, taken within the last six months at most. Your face should be clearly visible, your eyes open, and the photo should be taken against a white background.
4. An Unclear Purpose of Travel

When filling out the DS-160 form, it's important that the purpose of your trip be clearly and precisely described. Avoid vague or incorrect information, and make sure all details match your plans and the accompanying documents.
Always check that your answers are consistent, and be prepared to give thorough answers at the interview.
5. Ignoring the Confirmation Code

After filling out the DS-160 form, saving the Confirmation Page is essential. This document is an important part of your visa process, and without it, you won't be able to attend your interview at the consulate.
That's why, after completing the visa application, you should download and keep the full application in a safe place.
Summary

Filling out the DS-160 form requires attention and precision. Giving accurate and complete answers to every question is the guarantee of a successful visa application. Don't forget that any inaccurate information or careless approach may become a reason for refusal. Always double-check your information and prepare the necessary documentation.
